artifacts.summary: Measured meta catch-all inventory (25 meta-only / 86 meta-tagged, correcting the description's 123), concrete per-group hook proposals from the prerequisite's section 5, a checkable trimming rule, the four .tier call sites plus a Tier-4 fallthrough decision, the 2 broken agent names, and the verbatim validator baseline.

memory_candidates.content: In .claude context index censuses, distinguish three different jq predicates: key-presence (`.load_when|has("task_types")`), non-empty (`(.load_when.task_types//[])|length>0`), and contains-value (`(.load_when.task_types//[])|index("meta")`). A prior agent-system census reported '123 of 129 core entries carrying task_types:["meta"]' when it had actually measured key-presence; the true contains-"meta" count was 86, and 40 entries carried an empty task_types array. Always state which predicate a reported count used.

validate-context-budgets.sh's per-agent budget check counts ONLY load_when.agents matches -- it never reads load_when.task_types or load_when.commands. Consequence: trimming task_types hooks reduces what the documented adaptive context-discovery query actually loads, but moves the validator's reported per-agent token totals not at all. Any task whose verification bar is 'zero per-agent budget violations' must change load_when.agents breadth or the CAPS table; task_type trimming alone cannot satisfy it.

Core (always-loaded) index-entries.json must not name extension-owned agents in load_when.agents: when the extension is not loaded, the agent .md never reaches .claude/agents/ and the reference dangles. The established pattern is for the extension to declare its OWN index entry for the same core-owned file path with its own agents array (as lean/index-entries.json does for contracts/adversarial-verification.md). Caveat: this produces two entries for one path when the extension is loaded, so confirm loader dedup-by-path behavior before adding such an entry.
